text:
Erin (VP Eng): Thanks for coming to the runtime section of the all-hands. Two quick clarifications from leadership requested here: 1) how should teams think about kernel-v5 vs batching/caching priorities for their apps? 2) any concrete timeline or opt-in plan for Dedicated/Private customers? Keep replies short or use :point_down: bullets.

Devon (Runtime Lead): TL;DR: kernel-v5 = long-context tail-latency wins; batching/caching = cost & throughput wins for short requests. Well run both tracks in parallel with clear canaries.

Lina (Kernel Eng): Kernel detail in one line: v5 reorders attention loops and adds a fused rotary+QKV path that reduces p99 on long sequences by ~20% in our microbenchmarks (model dependent).

Priya (Infra PM): Dedicated/Private: customers will be able to opt into the canary for their clusters. No forced upgrades. We'll tag affected customers and share a per-customer rollout plan.

Marco (PM): Product note: teams owning interactive features (short <128 token calls) should prioritize batching tuning first; teams with long documents or retrieval-augmented flows should prioritize kernel-v5 migration guidance.

Devon (Runtime Lead): Short roadmap bullets:
- Week A: kernel-v5 correctness + cross-hardware smoke tests.
- Week B: small-scale canaries on internal services.
- Week C-D: public canaries + Dedicated opt-ins.
- Ongoing: batching/caching policy engine iterations (perf + unit-cost).

Lina (Kernel Eng): Risks: quant path divergence on some quantized 4-bit paths; memory fragmentation with larger KV caches. Rollback: kernel switch + model-variant routing to v4. Canary window target: 48h for internal, 72h for public.

ops-bot: Canary job created: canary/kernel-v5/242000. Auto-rollback triggers: p99 > baseline * 1.25 for 10m, or errors > 0.75% sustained for 5m.

Devon (Runtime Lead): Measurement: we'll publish p50/p95/p99 and token-cost deltas per-model in the RFC. Expect different numbers for 2k vs 32k contexts.

Priya (Infra PM): Ops checklist (short): create canary channel, assign SRE on-call, tag impacted customers, publish runbook link.

Erin (VP Eng): Action items: Devon - RFC + bench table; Priya - canary runbook + opt-in form; Lina - list known quant edge cases; Marco - flag product owners for short-request flows. Follow-up sync Fri 10am PT (30m).

Lina (Kernel Eng): Quick config example for teams that want to opt-in early (add to model route):
```json
{"kernel_preference": "v5", "opt_in_reason": "early perf testing", "slo_override": {"p99_ms": 1200}}
```

Devon (Runtime Lead): If anyone has a one-sentence blocker post now. Otherwise keep discussions in the RFC thread once posted.

Marco (PM): I'll compile a list of internal product owners for outreach and ping them in #product.

Erin (VP Eng): Great. Thanks all. Short blockers only please. End.
